question.problem:
$$
|\begin{aligned}9 & 8 & -4 & -3 \\ 5 & -4 & -1 & 3 \\ -3 & 0 & 1 & -1 \\ -2 & -6 & 4 & 2\end{aligned}|
$$

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

*Hint: Use elementary column operations to make the entries to the left of ${a}_{44}$ equal to zero.*
question.worked_solution:
Let's make entries to the left of ${a}_{44}=2$ equal to zero using elementary column operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}9 & 8 & -4 & -3 \\ 5 & -4 & -1 & 3 \\ -3 & 0 & 1 & -1 \\ -2 & -6 & 4 & 2\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}+{C}_{4} \\ {C}_{2}:={C}_{2}+3{C}_{4} \\ {C}_{3}:={C}_{3}+(-2){C}_{4}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}6 & -1 & 2 & -3 \\ 8 & 5 & -7 & 3 \\ -4 & -3 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $4$th row, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}6 & -1 & 2 & -3 \\ 8 & 5 & -7 & 3 \\ -4 & -3 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =2\cdot (-1)^{4+4}|\begin{aligned}6 & -1 & 2 \\ 8 & 5 & -7 \\ -4 & -3 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =2|\begin{aligned}6 & -1 & 2 \\ 8 & 5 & -7 \\ -4 & -3 & 3\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$
